chunks: And that which was narrated is: Ali ibn al-Hasan from Ahmad ibn al-Hasan from Amr ibn Sa'id from Musaddiq ibn Sadah from 'Ammar al-Sabati from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who has missed days from the month of Ramadan and wishes to make them up, when does he intend the fasting? He said: 'He has the choice until the sun sets. When the sun sets, if he intended fasting, let him fast; and if he intended breaking the fast, let him break it.'
He was asked: If he intended breaking the fast, is it appropriate for him to intend fasting after the sun has set? He said: 'No.'

He was asked: If he intended fasting and then broke the fast after the sun had set? He said: 'He has erred, and there is nothing upon him except the making up of that day which he intended to make up.'

His saying (peace be upon him) 'and there is nothing upon him except the making up of that day' is to be understood as meaning there is no punishment upon him, because whoever breaks the fast on this day does not deserve punishment, even if he breaks it after midday, and expiation (kaffarah) falls upon him as we have explained. It is not so for the one who breaks the fast in Ramadan, because he deserves punishment, making up, and expiation. As for voluntary fasting, he has the choice to break it at any time he wishes, and there is nothing upon him. Indicating this is what we have previously mentioned from the narrations, and clarifying it further is what was narrated:

key_terms.قَضَاءُ شَهْرِ رَمَضَانَ: Making up missed days of Ramadan

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for someone who intends to fast a missed Ramadan day but breaks it after midday?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* clarifies the juristic distinction between fasting for *qada* (making up missed days) and voluntary fasting, establishing that the intention (*niyyah*) remains valid until sunset. It highlights the Shia scholarly view that breaking fast after intending to fast in this context incurs no expiation (*kaffarah*), contrasting it with the stricter penalties for breaking fast during the holy month of Ramadan itself. The text further notes that for voluntary fasts, one may break the fast at any time without penalty, underscoring the flexibility of *qada* obligations.
